intro: If you're heading to Krabi and want somewhere quiet to sleep that isn't pricey, with a pool to cool off in, and you don't mind not stepping straight into the bustle the moment you walk out the door — The Chill at Krabi Hotel is a name that keeps coming up among Krabi's budget stays · It's a small boutique hotel with just 37 rooms, opened in 2017, set on the Pak Nam side, suburban Krabi, about 1.8 kilometres from the town centre · What real reviews consistently praise is the quiet, the comfortable beds, the clean rooms and the friendly staff, plus an outdoor pool and a kids' pool in the garden · But to be straight with you, you can't really walk anywhere from this location — you'll mostly need a car · From about THB 900/night, score 9.2 from 56 reviews on Trip.com

body.html: Who The Chill at Krabi suits — to put it as simply as possible, The Chill at Krabi Hotel is a small hotel for people who value "quiet and actually getting to rest" more than staying on a walking street or right by the sea · It's not a beachfront resort at Ao Nang, and it's not a social hostel in the middle of the market where you can step out and grab lunch in a minute · Instead it's a boutique hotel of just 37 rooms, open since 2017, set in the Pak Nam area, a suburban part of Mueang Krabi district · The overall feel is that of a quiet garden home, with trees, an outdoor pool and a seating area in the garden · Real reviews line up on this: the people it suits are couples who want a quiet, budget-friendly stay, families with their own car or a rental, and travellers using Krabi as a base before moving on to the islands or somewhere else — more than people who want to wander at night or step out to find streets full of restaurants · Another group that says they were impressed is people who just want to sleep deeply, because many reviews rank the beds here among the top highlights · You could say it lives up to the word "rest" in the name The Chill, but the trade-off is accepting that the location isn't in the middle of the action and that you'll need to plan your transport a little

Location and getting around — this is the thing to understand clearly before you book, because it's both a strength and a watch-out for The Chill at Krabi · The hotel is at 121 Watchara Road, Pak Nam, Mueang Krabi, on the suburban side, about 1.8 kilometres from central Krabi (the Chao Fah Pier area, the night market, Maharaj Road) · That's only a few minutes by car or motorbike, but it's fairly far to walk and there aren't many shops to stop at along the way — many foreign reviews say the same thing: "there's almost nothing within walking distance", so you'll mostly need a car · For longer trips: it's about 12 kilometres, or roughly an 18 min drive, from Krabi Airport (KBV), which is handy for people who fly in and want to reach the hotel without a long ride · Ao Nang beach is about 15 kilometres away, roughly a 25–30 min drive · An important note that reviews mention is that Grab-style ride services on this side aren't very reliable — sometimes cars are hard to find, so anyone who hasn't driven in needs to rely on the hotel's car service or a local taxi · The upside of a location like this is the quiet you can't get staying in town, plus free private parking — a great fit for anyone renting a car to explore Krabi and the surrounding province

"Slept really well because it's genuinely quiet — no traffic or crowd noise, and the bed was so soft I didn't want to get up · But I'll be honest, there's not much when you step outside; you need to call a car or have your own to get around comfortably."

Room types and decor — The Chill at Krabi has 37 rooms in total (34 air-conditioned), split into just a few easy-to-choose types · It starts with the Standard Twin Room (two single beds) and the Standard Double Room (one large bed), the entry-priced rooms, good for couples or travel companions on a budget · Step up to the Family Room, with one queen bed plus a sofa bed, which fits a small family or a group of three · And the room many people recommend is the Deluxe Double with Terrace, with a queen bed plus a private terrace that opens onto a garden or pool view · The decor is a simple, contemporary style in bright, easy-on-the-eye tones — not luxurious, but it looks clean and newer than you'd expect for the price · Every room has air conditioning, a flat-screen TV with satellite channels, hot water and free Wi-Fi · The thing real reviews praise most is the bed — one foreign guest even called it "the most comfortable bed I've slept in among all the places I've stayed across Thailand," and plenty of others say the rooms are clean, well kept and feel new · Worth knowing: some reviews mention a musty smell in the bathroom in some rooms and Wi-Fi that's sometimes slow, which is common in small hotels at this price · If a view and a private sitting area matter to you, paying a little extra for the Deluxe room with a terrace is worth it

Facilities and the pool — even though it's a small hotel, The Chill at Krabi has everything you need for an easy stay · The highlight is the outdoor pool in the garden, with a separate kids' pool, which puts families with little ones more at ease · Many reviews say the pool is clean and the area around it is quiet — good for lounging or a dip in the afternoon · One small note from a few reviews is that the pool water can be fairly heavily chlorinated at times, which is just normal upkeep, but people with sensitive skin may notice it · Besides the pool, there's a tropical garden and outdoor seating area that keep the overall feel green and shaded · The basics are all covered: free private parking, free Wi-Fi throughout, an in-house restaurant, room service, laundry service, luggage storage, a tour and transport desk, taxi booking, a lift, and a 24-hour front desk · There's also bike rental for anyone who wants to pedal around the area · To be straight, the pool and facilities here aren't big or resort-luxurious — they're sized to fit a small, budget-friendly hotel, but for cleanliness and quiet they punch above the price

Food and dining — the hotel has an in-house restaurant serving local food and simple dishes, and breakfast is available around 7:00 AM–10:00 AM (generally charged separately, depending on the promotion and room type you book — worth checking again when you reserve) · Reviews on the food are fairly mixed — some are happy with the freshly made, reasonably priced local dishes, while others say the breakfast presentation is still plain and the choices limited · There are also stretches when the restaurant isn't open every day, which is a limitation of a small hotel · Because the location is suburban and it's not easy to walk out to restaurants, many people suggest that if you stay here you should plan your meals ahead — for example, have a car to drive into town for places around Chao Fah Pier or Maharaj Road, or use food delivery · Overall, food isn't the reason to come here; it's a nice add-on for breakfast, and for other meals it's best to plan to head out

Service — service is the point The Chill at Krabi earns the most consistent praise for in real reviews · Many staff are described as friendly, kind and more thoughtful than you'd expect for a small hotel — one foreign review used the phrase "service minded" at a level that pleasantly surprised them · Because it's a small hotel, the staff can look after guests thoroughly, recognise faces, and help with calling cars, booking tours, or recommending where to eat and what to see · Many people say this is exactly what makes it feel warm and makes them want to come back, even if the location isn't the most convenient · One note that does come up: since the team is small to match the hotel's size, response can slow down a bit during busy periods or when several requests come in at once · But overall, service is a clear strength here

Voices from real reviews (praise and gripes) — pulling together Trip.com, Booking.com and Tripadvisor, the picture is fairly consistent · On the praise side: a quiet atmosphere that's easy to sleep in, soft and very comfortable beds (the most frequently mentioned point), clean rooms that look new with easy-on-the-eye tones, friendly and attentive staff, a clean pool with a shaded garden around it, and good value for what you get · On the watch-out side: the most-mentioned issue is the suburban location where you can't really walk anywhere, needing a car, and unreliable ride services on this side · Next come Wi-Fi that's sometimes slow, a musty smell in the bathroom in some rooms, breakfast that's still plain in look and choice, and pool water that's fairly heavily chlorinated at times · Most of these gripes are manageable by setting expectations right from the start — if you understand you're booking a small, budget-friendly hotel that sells quiet, not an in-town stay you can walk around from, most people end up satisfied

"Clean room, lovely staff, cheap but more than worth it, and the pool is good · The only downsides are the internet's a bit slow and you really need a car because it's so quiet around here with no shops to walk to — next time I'll rent a car myself."

Price and value — the entry price for a Standard room is about THB 900/night in normal pricing (around US$27), with an average of roughly THB 1,700–1,800/night (around US$53) depending on the season and room type · During Krabi's high season or long holidays, prices can climb to around THB 2,000–2,500+ · Compared with similar-level stays in central Krabi, The Chill's selling point is getting a pool, a garden, free parking and quiet at a price lower than many in-town hotels · The clear trade-off is a location that needs a car, or paying to get into town every time · If you're already renting a car to explore Krabi, or using Krabi as a quiet base before heading on to the islands, every baht you spend pays off · But if you don't have a car and you plan to walk the night market or eat at restaurants in town every meal, the extra transport cost you'll pay daily could cancel out the savings on the room — factor that in before you decide

Good to know before you book — a few things make the stay smoother · One, if you're not driving in, plan your transport ahead — ask about the hotel's transfer or car service, because Grab is hard to find on this side · Two, if a view and a sitting area matter to you, choose the Deluxe Double with Terrace, which has a private terrace · Three, check at booking whether breakfast is included in the room rate or charged separately, and which days the restaurant is open, since some stretches it isn't open every day · Four, if you're sensitive to smells or particular about the bathroom, ask to have the room aired out before check-in and choose a freshly cleaned room · Five, during Krabi's high season (November–April) prices rise and rooms fill up fast, so book ahead and compare prices across several platforms · Six, pick free cancellation if your plans aren't set, since prices tend to shift with the season

The verdict — from all the real reviews, The Chill at Krabi Hotel is the best fit for people who want a quiet, clean, budget-friendly stay with a pool in Krabi, who have their own car or are ready to plan their transport · The beds that earn special praise, the quiet you can't get with an in-town stay, the garden pool, free parking, and friendly staff make it good value among budget options · If you're looking for a stay right on Ao Nang beach, or you want to step out of your room straight into restaurants and the night market, this may not be the answer, and you should consider a stay in the Ao Nang area or central Krabi town instead · But for a trip where you genuinely want to rest, on a budget you can manage, and you don't mind getting around by car — The Chill at Krabi is a small option that does its job well, true to its name, and it's why the review scores stay high

honestSummary: The Chill at Krabi Hotel is the best choice for people who want to stay somewhere quiet, clean and with a pool on a budget, with a car or ready to plan their transport — beds that earn praise, hard-to-find quiet, a garden pool, and friendly staff · But you have to accept that the location is suburban with little within walking distance, Wi-Fi is sometimes slow, and it's a small hotel where food is a secondary point
honestChecks: If you don't have a car and want to walk around town — this is on the suburban Pak Nam side, about 1.8 km from town, hard to walk anywhere and Grab is scarce → consider a stay in central Krabi town or the Chao Fah Pier area instead

If you want to stay right on Ao Nang beach — this is an in-town hotel on the suburban side, not a beachfront resort; Ao Nang is about 15 km away → choose a stay in the Ao Nang area if you want to walk to the beach

If you need fast internet and full resort-style facilities — it's a small hotel, Wi-Fi is sometimes slow and the facilities are right-sized → set your expectations around quiet, cleanliness and value above all

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — The Chill at Krabi Hotel

faq.q: Where is The Chill at Krabi Hotel · what can you walk to?
faq.a: The hotel is at 121 Watchara Road, Pak Nam, Mueang Krabi, on the suburban side, about 1.8 km from central Krabi town and around 12 km from Krabi Airport (about an 18 min drive) · To be straight, this area is quiet and you can't really walk anywhere — you'll need a car, and Grab is scarce on this side, so it suits people who have a car or are ready to plan their transport

faq.q: What's the starting price at The Chill at Krabi Hotel · what room types are there?
faq.a: Prices start at about THB 900/night for a Standard room in normal pricing, with an average of roughly THB 1,700–1,800 · There are Standard Twin, Standard Double, Family Room (queen bed + sofa bed) and Deluxe Double with Terrace, which has a private terrace · During high season (Nov–Apr) prices rise, so it's worth comparing several platforms before booking

faq.q: Who is The Chill at Krabi Hotel good for?
faq.a: It's a great fit for couples and small families who want a quiet, budget-friendly stay and have their own car, or who use Krabi as a resting point before heading on to the islands · There's a pool and garden to relax in, and comfortable beds · If you want to walk around the town centre or stay right on Ao Nang beach, a stay in another area may suit you better

faq.q: Does The Chill at Krabi Hotel have a pool and breakfast?
faq.a: Yes, there's an outdoor pool with a kids' pool in a tropical garden, with a quiet atmosphere, and reviews say the pool is clean · Breakfast is available around 7:00 AM–10:00 AM (often charged separately, worth checking at booking), and the restaurant isn't open every day in some stretches · Reviews on the food are fairly mixed, so it's best to plan your other meals

faq.q: What are the Wi-Fi and parking like at The Chill at Krabi?
faq.a: There's free Wi-Fi throughout, but some reviews say the signal is sometimes slow · The free private parking is an advantage, good for anyone renting a car to explore Krabi, making it much easier to get into town and out to the beaches

faq.q: What should you know before booking The Chill at Krabi?
faq.a: Mainly, plan your transport well because the location is suburban and Grab is scarce · Check whether breakfast is included in the rate or charged separately, and which days the restaurant is open · If you're sensitive to smells, ask to have the room aired out and choose a freshly cleaned one · Choose a room with a terrace if a view matters to you, and book ahead during high season
